bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

import subprocess, json

    r=subprocess.run(['./executable',f,'--error-format','json'],capture_output=True,text=True)

for f in ['/tmp/c/s7.sol','/tmp/c/s21.sol','/tmp/c/s19.sol']:

    print('=====',f, open(f).read().rstrip())
    print('JSON primary', d['sourceLocation'])
    for s in d['secondarySourceLocations']: print('  sec', s)
    print(err)
    for l in err.split('\n'):
        if '^' in l or '-' in l:
            i=min([l.index(c) for c in set(l) if c in '^-'])
            print('   markers at src offset', i-4, 'len', len(l)-i)
EOF

    pub fn display_text(&self, start: usize, end: usize) -> String {
        let s = &self.text[start.min(self.text.len())..end.min(self.text.len())];
        let mut out = String::new();
        let mut w = 0usize;
        for c in s.chars() {
            if c == '\t' {
                let n = 4 - (w % 4);
                for _ in 0..n {
                    out.push(' ');
                }
                w += n;
            } else if (c as u32) < 0x20 || c as u32 == 0x7f {
                let cp = c as u32;
                let pic = char::from_u32(0x2400 + cp).unwrap_or(c);
                out.push(pic);
                w += 1;
            } else {
                out.push(c);
                w += char_width(c);
            }
        }

    }

impl Renderer {
    fn st(&self, code: &str, text: &str) -> String {
        if !self.color || text.is_empty() {
            return text.to_string();
        }
        format!("{}{}{}m{}{}", BOLD, "\x1b[", code, text, RESET)
    }

    fn sev_code(&self, s: Severity) -> &'static str {
        match s {
            Severity::Error => "91",
            Severity::Warning => "93",
            Severity::Note => "92",
        }
    }

    fn gch(&self) -> &str {
        match self.style {
            HumanStyle::Unicode => "│",
            _ => "|",
        }
    }

    fn gutter(&self, digits: usize) -> String {
        format!("{}{}", " ".repeat(digits + 1), self.st("94", self.gch()))
    }

cd /workspace && python3 - <<'PY'
for line in open('/tmp/cli_short.txt'):
    line=line.rstrip('\n')
    if line.startswith('  ') and ('--' in line or ' -' in line):
        i=0
        while i < len(line) and line[i]==' ': i+=1
        # find the start of the help text (after the flag)
        # locate the end of the flag: the flag is the first token(s)
        j=line.find('  ', i)
        name=line[:j]
        help_=line[j:].strip()
        print(len(name), repr(name), '|', len(line)-j-len(line[j:].lstrip()), repr(help_[:30]))
PY

    fn parse_type_kind(&mut self) -> TypeKind {
        let t = self.cur().clone();
        let start = t.span;
        if t.is_kw("mapping") {
            self.bump();
            if !self.eat_punct("(") {
                self.expected(Exp::Tok("("));
                self.bail(&[";", "}"]);
                return TypeKind::Mapping(
                    Box::new(Type { span: start, kind: Box::new(TypeKind::Elementary(ElementaryType::Uint(256))) }),
                    Box::new(Type { span: start, kind: Box::new(TypeKind::Elementary(ElementaryType::Uint(256))) }),
                );
            }
            let key = self.parse_mapping_key_type();
            if !self.eat_punct("=>") {
                self.expected_one_of(&[Exp::Tok("=>"), Exp::Tok("["), Exp::Tok("payable"), Exp::Tok("pure"), Exp::Tok("view"), TOK_IDENT]);
            }
            let value = self.parse_mapping_value_type();
            if !self.eat_punct(")") {
                self.expected(Exp::Tok(")"));
            }
            return TypeKind::Mapping(Box::new(key), Box::new(value));
        }
        if t.is_kw("function") {
            self.bump();
            let params = if self.at_punct("(") {
                self.parse_param_list(false)
            } else {
                self.expected(Exp::Tok("("));
                vec![]
            };
            let mut visibility = None;
            let mut mutability = None;
            let mut returns: Vec<Param> = vec![];
            loop {
                if self.at_kw("returns") {
                    self.bump();
                    returns = self.parse_param_list(true);
                    continue;
                }
